newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Bank Negara says few banks exceed lending limits.
newsitem.headline: Bank Negara says few banks exceed lending limits.

text.p: Malaysia's central bank said on Tuesday that "not many" banks have exceeded new limits on lending to the broad property and share market sectors.
"It is not an industry-wide issue," said Bank Negara deputy governor Fong Weng Phak. "There were a number but not that many."

At a press briefing to clarify the curbs the bank announced on March 28, Fong said the stock market had "over-reacted" to the new limits. These require banks to trim their exposure to the broad property sector to 20 percent of total outstanding loans. New restrictions were also placed on lending for stocks and shares.
"I think people have over-reacted without understanding the measures," Fong said. "I think we have explained the measures and some of the implications."
He said the Banking Act contained penalties if banks do not ultimately conform with the new limits, but added that the central bank would use "moral suasion" to ensure compliance.
Theme parks and hotel resorts are exempt -- but not any housing project associated with them. Golf courses, on the other hand, fall under the limits.
Lending for purchase of shares in an initial public offering fall under the new limits, except in the case of manufacturing and infrastructure companies.
Employee stock option plans are also exempt.
"We need to look at it on a case-by-case basis," Fong said.
He stressed that the implementation of the new limits would be flexible. Malasysia's strong economic growth means compliance can take place in a non-crisis atmosphere over time, he said.
Banks and finance companies "have to work out their own plans and strategy" for compliance, Fong said.
The lending limits have a number of exemptions, he explained. Owner-occupied housing loans would be exempted under the curbs aimed at dampening speculation in the market.

The property lending curbs exempt medium and low-cost housing -- 150,000 ringgit and below. If, for example, 40 percent of a mixed development project is low cost housing, that percentage would be exempted from a bank's lending to that project, Fong said.
"We have the luxury of time," Fong said.
The intention of the new limits is to reallocate resources away from property, shares and consumption to the manufacturing and production sector.
About 17 percent of total loans in the banking system is for the manufacturing sector, while nearly 30 percent is allocated to the broad property sector, according to central bank figures.

"The spirit of the regulations is not to plug all loopholes," Fong said. "The spirit is to send a message to the country about allocating resources to the production sector and prevent the build-up of an asset bubble."
